cues.en: So we're gonna
cues.zh: 所以我们要

cues.en: give a quick shout out to Rogue from 1980 because we really wouldn't be here without it.
cues.zh: 快速致敬 1980 年的《Rogue》，因为没有它，我们真的不会走到这里。

cues.en: It's one of the seminal
cues.zh: 它是开创性的

cues.en: and first uses of procedural generation that really defines the genre. It splats out up to nine rooms, connects them randomly.
cues.zh: 也是最早使用程序化生成的作品之一，真正定义了这个品类。它会生成最多九个房间，并随机连接它们。

cues.en: Anyway,
cues.zh: 总之，

cues.en: it's been said that they did that because they needed to keep the game small and couldn't really fit in 50 beautifully hand designed levels.
cues.zh: 据说他们这样做是因为需要把游戏做小，实在塞不进 50 个精美手工设计的关卡。

cues.en: But really, that created one of the strengths of the genre in the first place. When you start a new game, you have a different map every time.
cues.zh: 但实际上，这恰恰造就了这个类型的一大优势。每次开新游戏，地图都不同。

cues.en: So every time you play, instead of memorizing that I need to go up, up, up, right,
cues.zh: 所以每次游玩时，你不再死记我要往上、往上、往上、往右，

cues.en: you're learning instead that I should interact this way with different monsters, interact this way with rooms, navigate like this, learning the system rather than learning the game itself, giving you effectively infinite replay.
cues.zh: 而是学会以这种方式与不同怪物交互、以这种方式与房间交互、这样导航，学的是系统而不是游戏本身，从而带来几乎无限的重玩性。

cues.en: Also, any talk on Proc Gen really has to mention Dwarf Fortress because no other Proc Gen game has ever managed to cram this much procedural generation into one binary.
cues.zh: 另外，任何关于程序化生成的演讲都必须提到 Dwarf Fortress，因为还没有其他程序化生成游戏能把这么多程序化生成内容塞进一个二进制文件里。

cues.en: If you haven't played it, go out and do so. Support them on Steam and
cues.zh: 如果你还没玩过，去玩玩吧。在 Steam 上支持他们，并

cues.en: tell them how awesome they are. They
cues.zh: 告诉他们他们有多棒。他们

cues.en: generate everything from a massive overworld with sweeping mountain ranges, dense forests, volcanoes, demon infested fortresses,
cues.zh: 生成一切：从拥有连绵山脉、茂密森林、火山、恶魔盘踞堡垒的巨大世界地图，

cues.en: fill it up with procedurally generated civilizations who either like or hate each other. And then you can drill down all the way down to Eurost and find out which procedurally generated deity he worships, which procedurally generated tavern he drinks in, and learn all about his quest to cross the land and find the perfect sock.
cues.zh: 再填满程序化生成的文明，它们彼此或喜欢或憎恨。然后你可以一路下钻到 Eurost，查明他崇拜哪位程序化生成的神祇、在哪家程序化生成的酒馆喝酒，并了解他穿越大地寻找完美袜子的全部任务。

cues.en: At the midscale, you can zoom into any particular land block on the map, find that it is beautifully rendered, still matches the
cues.zh: 在中尺度上，你可以放大地图上的任何特定地块，发现它渲染得很精美，仍然与上方

cues.en: overall shape of the overworld above it. The trees gain foliage, lose foliage, depending on their type and the type spawns appropriate to the biome. In other words, there is pretty much every Proc Gen technique that you can think of in this game. Hang out on the Bay twelve forums, and that is a great place to learn about them.
cues.zh: 主世界的整体形状相符。树木会根据类型获得或失去枝叶，并且按生物群系生成合适的类型。换句话说，这款游戏里几乎有你所能想到的每一种程序化生成技术。去逛逛 Bay 12 论坛，那里是学习这些技术的好地方。

cues.en: So, one thing that's clear from both of these games is that while they're random, the randomness doesn't define the game. The randomness is fed into an algorithm that generates something that approximates what you want to get, but ensures that it's different every time.
cues.zh: 所以，从这两款游戏中可以清楚看到一件事：尽管它们是随机的，但随机性并不定义游戏。随机性被输入到一个算法中，生成接近你想要的结果，同时确保每次都不同。

cues.en: So we're going to start looking at some algorithms for doing that.
cues.zh: 所以我们要开始看一些实现这一点的算法。

cues.en: Simple room placement. If you've done any of the roguelike development tutorials, then you've seen this one.
cues.zh: 简单的房间放置。如果你做过任何 roguelike 开发教程，那你一定见过这个。

cues.en: You start with a solid map. You pick a random rectangle.
cues.zh: 你从一张实心地图开始。你随机选一个矩形。

cues.en: If there isn't a room already there, you fill in the rectangle.
cues.zh: 如果那里还没有房间，你就填充这个矩形。

cues.en: You keep adding rooms until you meet whatever criteria you've come up with for enough.
cues.zh: 你不断添加房间，直到满足你设定的“足够”标准。

cues.en: And then you join the rooms together with corridors. Let's watch this in action.
cues.zh: 然后用走廊把房间连接起来。让我们看看实际运行效果。

cues.en: As you can see, it's placing rooms randomly. When you see the red rectangles with the exclamation marks, try to generate one that overlaps, so you have to discard it and try again.
cues.zh: 如你所见，它在随机放置房间。当你看到带感叹号的红色矩形时，那是试着生成一个重叠的房间，所以你必须丢弃它并重试。

cues.en: And then it joins them together with corridors. In this case, I went with a simple dogleg algorithm
cues.zh: 然后把它们用走廊连接起来。这里我用了简单的折线算法

cues.en: that randomly switches between being either vertical first or horizontal first.
cues.zh: 随机在优先垂直或优先水平之间切换。

cues.en: That's pretty much exactly the algorithm from the Python roguelike
cues.zh: 这基本就是Python roguelike

cues.en: dev tutorial that
cues.zh: 开发教程里的那个算法

cues.en: the roguelike dev subreddit
cues.zh: 也就是roguelike开发subreddit

cues.en: recommends that you start with.
cues.zh: 推荐入门用的那个。

cues.en: So a good refinement of that is binary space partition rooms,
cues.zh: 在此基础上一个很好的改进是二叉空间分割房间，

cues.en: or BSP.
cues.zh: 也就是BSP。

cues.en: Binary space partition is fancy developer torque for chopping in half.
cues.zh: 二叉空间分割是开发者圈子里对“对半切”的花哨说法。

cues.en: It gives a similar result to random room placement, but it pretty much guarantees that everything is better spaced out. You'll find that it's used in NetHack amongst other games.
cues.zh: 它的结果和随机放置房间类似，但基本能保证所有东西间距更合理。你会发现NetHack等游戏都用了它。

cues.en: So to do BSP,
cues.zh: 要做BSP，

cues.en: you divide your map in half. And you randomly decide whether you want to divide
cues.zh: 就把地图对半分。然后随机决定是

cues.en: vertically or horizontally, and divide that half in half. Then you keep dividing your halves all the way down until you have a space that's roughly the right size you want to use for a room. I personally like to then add a gutter of one tile around it to ensure that you don't get rooms joining together, unless that's what you want.
cues.zh: 垂直还是水平切，再把那一半对半分。接着不断把各半继续切下去，直到得到大致适合做房间的大小。我个人喜欢再在周围留一格边距，确保房间不会连在一起，除非你就想要那样。

cues.en: So watching that in action,
cues.zh: 看它实际运行起来，

cues.en: you see that there's absolutely no rejections,
cues.zh: 你会发现完全没有被拒绝的情况，

cues.en: the rooms are nicely spaced out,
cues.zh: 房间间距很合理，

cues.en: and you wind up with a pretty usable map.
cues.zh: 最后得到一张相当可用的地图。

cues.en: So a complete change of gear, Cellular Automata.
cues.zh: 接下来彻底换个思路，元胞自动机。

cues.en: I personally love this one because it involves an ordered looking natural map from complete chaos.
cues.zh: 我个人很喜欢这个，因为它能从完全的混沌中生成看起来有序、自然的地图。

cues.en: I said you don't always start with complete random. Well, this one you do. You can literally
cues.zh: 我说过不一定非要从完全随机开始。好吧，这个确实要。你可以直接

cues.en: make half your map walls, half your map floors
cues.zh: 把地图一半做成墙，一半做成地板

cues.en: randomly picked, no chance of getting through it. And you'll end up with something that you can use.
cues.zh: 随机选取，不可能走通。最后你会得到能用的东西。

cues.en: If you've played Conway's Game of Life or seen articles about it, it's the same principle here. So once you've got your map, you make a copy of it, you iterate every tile that isn't on the edge, and count the number of neighbors, including diagonals.
cues.zh: 如果你玩过康威生命游戏或看过相关文章，原理是一样的。拿到地图后，复制一份，遍历每个非边缘格子，数邻居数量，包括对角线。

cues.en: If
cues.zh: 如果

cues.en: there are no neighbors, then you become a wall. If there's one to four neighbors, become empty. Five or more neighbors, become a wall. Now, you can and should tweak these rules to suit your game.
cues.zh: 没有邻居，就变成墙。有一到四个邻居，变成空地。五个或更多邻居，变成墙。现在你可以也应该调整这些规则来适配你的游戏。

cues.en: And watch this in action. Completely random soup quickly turns into a far more natural looking
cues.zh: 看看实际效果。完全随机的汤很快变成看起来自然得多的

cues.en: structure that
cues.zh: 结构，

cues.en: can actually be turned into a pretty useful map.
cues.zh: 能变成相当有用的地图。

cues.en: It's a really simple algorithm, really fast.
cues.zh: 算法非常简单，非常快。

cues.en: And given the same seed, you get the same result every time.
cues.zh: 给定相同的种子，每次结果都一样。

cues.en: Next one to talk about is Drunkard's Walk. This is another popular one for beginners.
cues.zh: 下一个要讲的是醉汉漫步。这是另一个适合初学者的流行算法。

cues.en: So the basic principle of Drunkard's Walk is that you start with a solid map, Find one Umbra Hulk and play it with beer until he's staggering randomly.
cues.zh: 醉汉漫步的基本原理是，从一张实心地图开始，找一个Umbra Hulk，灌他啤酒直到他随机踉跄。

cues.en: Place him somewhere on the map. As he staggers, he randomly smashes through walls
cues.zh: 把他放在地图某处。他踉跄时，随机砸穿墙壁

cues.en: and carving out a map. Don't bother worrying about whether he backtracks.
cues.zh: 开凿出地图。不用担心他是否走回头路。

cues.en: Let him stagger wherever he wants.
cues.zh: 让他随意蹒跚而行。

cues.en: Pick a maximum distance for him to travel, if, or her, I'm really not sure how Umbra Hulk gender works.
cues.zh: 给他或她设定一个最大移动距离，我实在不确定 Umbra Hulk 的性别机制是怎么运作的。

cues.en: If they travel too far, they pass out. And you pick another Umbra Hulk, spawn them somewhere within the open map,
cues.zh: 如果它们走得太远，就会昏过去。然后你再选另一个 Umbra Hulk，在开放地图的某处生成它，

cues.en: and let them smash.
cues.zh: 让它去砸。

cues.en: And then you stop spawning hulks when enough of your map is open. In this case, I've used one third of the map.
cues.zh: 当地图开放到足够程度时，就停止生成 hulk。在这个例子中，我用了三分之一的地图。

cues.en: So, watching this in action, you can see that each hulk is staggering completely randomly,
cues.zh: 所以，看实际效果，你可以看到每个 hulk 完全是随机蹒跚的，

cues.en: carving out more and more of the map. One big advantage of this is that you can guarantee
cues.zh: 不断开出越来越多的地图区域。这么做的一大优势是，你能保证

cues.en: that your map will be contiguous. It won't generate any areas that your player can't reach.
cues.zh: 地图是连通的。不会生成玩家无法到达的区域。

cues.en: It tends to give you a map that looks like it was carved out by water. It's ideal for creating limestone caverns and similar.
cues.zh: 它倾向于生成一张看起来像被水流冲刷出来的地图。非常适合做石灰岩洞穴之类的。

cues.en: Another algorithm, Diffusion Limited Aggregation.
cues.zh: 另一种算法，扩散限制凝聚。

cues.en: I highly recommend the Rogue Basin article on this one.
cues.zh: 我强烈推荐 Rogue Basin 上关于这个算法的文章。

cues.en: So for the simple version of this, you start by digging out a small target seed.
cues.zh: 简单版的做法是，先挖出一个小目标种子。

cues.en: And then you pick a random point anywhere on the map, a random direction, and shoot a particle.
cues.zh: 然后在地图上任意位置、任意方向选一个随机点，发射一个粒子。

cues.en: If you're really lucky, the particle will hit one of the already open areas. If it doesn't, you keep shooting until you hit something,
cues.zh: 如果运气好，粒子会撞上已经开放的区域。如果没撞上，就继续发射，直到撞到东西，

cues.en: something I've heard from a lot of military friends.
cues.zh: 这话我从很多军方朋友那儿听过。

cues.en: In the event that you do hit a target area,
cues.zh: 如果你确实撞到了目标区域，

cues.en: then you carve out the last solid area that you passed through. This tends to give you a very winding open map. Again, it's guaranteed to be contiguous.
cues.zh: 就把你最后穿过的那个实心区域挖开。这往往会给你一张非常蜿蜒的开放地图。同样，它能保证连通性。

cues.en: And there's a lot of ways that you can tweak the algorithm to make something more interesting.
cues.zh: 有很多方法可以调整算法，让生成的东西更有趣。

cues.en: So the central attractor is much more likely to always hit the target.
cues.zh: 所以中心吸引点更有可能总是命中目标。

cues.en: You randomly spawn your starting point, and then shoot the particle directly at the middle of the map. This pretty much ensures that you get an open space in the middle, ideal, for example, for you to put a dragon with this horde,
cues.zh: 你随机生成起点，然后直接把粒子射向地图中心。这基本能保证中间有一片开阔空间，比如正好适合你放一条龙和它的部落，

cues.en: and then a more interesting pattern forming around the edges,
cues.zh: 然后边缘会形成更有趣的图案，

cues.en: which could be where the Hobbit would lurk while he torments the poor dragon.
cues.zh: 那里可能正是霍比特人潜伏的地方，同时折磨着那条可怜的龙。

cues.en: On the right, you can see what happens if we use the same central attractor algorithm,
cues.zh: 在右边，你可以看到如果我们使用同样的中心吸引算法会发生什么，

cues.en: but simply apply symmetry down the vertical.
cues.zh: 但只是沿垂直方向应用对称。

cues.en: You start to get maps that look a lot like they either want to eat you, or maybe it's a butterfly,
cues.zh: 你开始得到的地图看起来要么想吃了你，要么也许是只蝴蝶，

cues.en: maybe it's a space invaders character.
cues.zh: 也许是太空侵略者里的角色。

cues.en: I recommend using this one sparingly,
cues.zh: 我建议这个要少用，

cues.en: but a bit of symmetry like that can be applied to any algorithm when you want to produce something that looks a lot less random.
cues.zh: 但当你想要生成看起来不那么随机的东西时，这种对称性可以应用到任何算法上。

cues.en: Another
cues.zh: 另一个

cues.en: algorithm that everyone should have in their toolkit is the Voronoi diagram.
cues.zh: 每个人都应该放进工具箱的算法是Voronoi图。

cues.en: So to make one of these, I do recommend googling it. You randomly or deliberately
cues.zh: 要做一个这样的图，我建议你直接谷歌一下。你随机或刻意地

cues.en: place seeds all over your map. You'd randomly place them if you just want to produce something random. If you place them very deliberately, for example, you can equally space them all over the map, you can produce something that looks very, very much like a beehive.
cues.zh: 在地图上到处放置种子点。如果你只想要随机效果，就随机放置。如果你非常刻意地放置，比如让它们在地图上均匀分布，你就能生成非常像蜂巢的东西。

cues.en: And then you iterate every point on the map,
cues.zh: 然后你遍历地图上的每个点，

cues.en: and it joins the
cues.zh: 它会并入

cues.en: area belonging to the closest seed.
cues.zh: 距离最近的种子点所属的区域。

cues.en: There are various fancy algorithms like Delaney triangulation to do this quickly. In the source code I've provided, I just brute forced it and did it the hard way.
cues.zh: 有很多花哨的算法能快速完成这件事，比如 Delaunay 三角剖分。在我提供的源码里，我只是用暴力方式硬算的。

cues.en: Now, one neat trick for customizing what you get is that you can use a different distance algorithm to determine which
cues.zh: 定制结果的一个巧妙技巧是，你可以用不同的距离算法来决定

cues.en: group every
cues.zh: 每个

cues.en: tile joins. So, on the left, I've used Pythagoras,
cues.zh: 格子并入哪个分组。所以左边我用了勾股距离，

cues.en: and it gives you relatively
cues.zh: 它给出的边缘相对

cues.en: smooth edges.
cues.zh: 平滑。

cues.en: Using Manhattan distance, which is the
cues.zh: 用曼哈顿距离，也就是

cues.en: same distance that you'd get if you ask a New York taxi driver how far
cues.zh: 你问纽约出租车司机去某地有多远时得到的距离——

cues.en: it is to get to somewhere, number of blocks north plus number of blocks east, gives you a much more
cues.zh: 向北几个街区加上向东几个街区——会给你一个更加

cues.en: man made looking sharp edged structure.
cues.zh: 像人造的、棱角分明的结构。

cues.en: And Chebyshev is a similar distance
cues.zh: 而切比雪夫是一种类似的距离

cues.en: algorithm and tends to give you somewhere in between the two.
cues.zh: 算法，结果往往介于两者之间。

cues.en: So what can you do with Fournier diagrams?
cues.zh: 那么用 Voronoi 图能做什么呢？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 你

cues.en: first thing you can do with them is find the edges,
cues.zh: 首先能做的是找出边缘，

cues.en: place walls there, and wind up with an alien cell structure.
cues.zh: 在那里放墙，最后得到一个异星牢房般的结构。

cues.en: Another good thing to do is decide that when you're spawning monsters,
cues.zh: 另一个好用法是，当你生成怪物时，

cues.en: you'll spawn the monsters together within a Voronaya cell.
cues.zh: 决定在同一个 Voronoi 格子里一起生成怪物。

cues.en: So if, for example, you've decided that the orc king should always be associated with his retinue,
cues.zh: 所以，比如你决定兽人国王总是要和他的随从待在一起，

cues.en: then you should probably spawn them in the same cell together, if possible.
cues.zh: 那可能就该尽量把他们生成在同一个格子里。

cues.en: Likewise,
cues.zh: 同样，

cues.en: if you've decided that orcs must never in fact be near dark elves, make sure that you spawn them in far away cells.
cues.zh: 如果你决定兽人绝不能靠近黑暗精灵，那就确保把他们生成在相距很远的格子里。

cues.en: You can also use this for very effective city generation.
cues.zh: 你也可以用它来高效生成城市。

cues.en: In my proc jam
cues.zh: 在我的 proc jam 上

cues.en: game, Apocalypse Taxi, I used the edges of Varnai cells to determine where the roads went, and then randomly populated the content of each cell with something like heavy industrial city, light industrial,
cues.zh: 游戏《Apocalypse Taxi》中，我用Varnai单元的边界来确定道路走向，然后随机为每个单元填充内容，比如重工业城市、轻工业区，

cues.en: and it worked pretty well.
cues.zh: 而且效果还挺不错的。

cues.en: Combined with other techniques, this can be extremely useful.
cues.zh: 结合其他技术，这会非常有用。

cues.en: So the next one up is Perlin and simplex noise, which is used all over the place, more
cues.zh: 接下来是 Perlin 噪声和 simplex 噪声，它们的应用非常广泛，而且

cues.en: than you might think.
cues.zh: 比你想象的要容易。

cues.en: So Perlin and simplex noise are basically a bunch of gradients
cues.zh: Perlin噪声和simplex噪声基本上就是一堆梯度

cues.en: combined together with a few variables we'll talk about in a moment.
cues.zh: 与几个我们稍后会讨论的变量结合在了一起。

cues.en: You can generate it in two or three dimensions. If you
cues.zh: 你可以从两个或三个维度来生成它。如果你

cues.en: look at an x y value, it gives you a number between minus one and one.
cues.zh: 看一个 x y 值，它会给你一个介于负一和一之间的数。

cues.en: And the nice thing is, if you look at an adjacent one, it will
cues.zh: 好处是，如果你看相邻的一个，它会

cues.en: be smoothly moving either up or down
cues.zh: 要能平稳地向上或向下移动

cues.en: relative to the neighboring squares. It's also continuous. So, if you decide to look from
cues.zh: 相对于相邻的方格。它也是连续的。所以，如果你决定从……来看

cues.en: x's one
cues.zh: x 的那个

cues.en: through two,
cues.zh: 到第二点，

cues.en: and then decide to zoom in to 1.5 through two, you'll actually get exactly the same shape as you saw on the right hand side of the first one.
cues.zh: 然后决定放大到1.5到2倍，你实际上会得到与第一个图形右侧所见完全相同的形状。

cues.en: So what do the variables mean? The number of octaves is how many different gradients it's mixing in. Gain is how long various
cues.zh: 那么这些变量是什么意思？八度数指的是它混合了多少种不同的渐变。增益则是指各种

cues.en: gradients last. Lacunarity adds in randomness.
cues.zh: 梯度最后再说。空隙度增加了随机性。等等，我想先讲梯度。间隙度（Lacunarity）增添了随机性。

cues.en: And as you can see from the picture
cues.zh: 从图中可以看到

cues.en: on the right hand side, which I guess is
cues.zh: 右边这个，我猜是

cues.en: my left,
cues.zh: 在我左边，

cues.en: this starts to feather it in, make it look a lot more random.
cues.zh: 这样就开始把它羽化融入，看起来更加随机了。

cues.en: And frequency is how frequently each of the various octaves peaks.
cues.zh: 而频率是指各个八度峰值出现的频繁程度。

cues.en: So what I recommend you do is find a Perlin on simplex noise tool and simply play with these values until you get something that you like. So what can you do with them? The answer is actually quite a lot.
cues.zh: 所以我建议你找一个 Perlin 或单纯形噪声工具，随便调这些值，直到调出你喜欢的效果。那能用它们做什么呢？答案其实相当多。

cues.en: The most common use is to make an overworld.
cues.zh: 最常见的用途是生成主世界。

cues.en: Because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: deterministic by random seed, every time you use the same seed, you get the same map.
cues.zh: 由随机种子决定，每次用同一个种子，你都会得到同一张地图。

cues.en: What I've done here is
cues.zh: 我在这里做的是

cues.en: altitudes from minus one to zero are blued out as water. Altitudes from zero to point seven five are in green, shaded as terrain.
cues.zh: 把负一到零的高度涂成蓝色作为水。零到零点七五的高度涂成绿色，作为地形着色。

cues.en: Altitudes above that are marked as mountains. And this is very common. You'll find this used in a lot of games. And as I mentioned, you can zoom in. So, as you zoom in, you start to see more of the gradient. The problem is
cues.zh: 高于这个高度的标为山脉。这很常见，很多游戏里都能见到。而且正如我提到的，你可以放大。放大后，你就能看到更多渐变细节。问题是

cues.en: that the gradients are actually kind of dull.
cues.zh: 这些渐变其实有点单调。

cues.en: And you can fix that. The best way to fix that is to make a second layer of noise. So, in this case, we've got a second layer of noise that is much more bumpy, has much more
cues.zh: 你可以解决这个问题。最好的办法是再加一层噪声。所以这里我们加了第二层噪声，它更加起伏，细节

cues.en: fine grained detail, but looks terrible as a continent as a whole. And then, as you zoom in,
cues.zh: 更精细，但作为整体大陆看效果很糟。然后，当你放大时，

cues.en: you change the percentage of each of the two gradients that you're mixing together.
cues.zh: 你调整两层渐变混合时的各自占比。

cues.en: So, when you're zoomed all the way out like that, you're seeing the relatively coherent overworld.
cues.zh: 所以，当你像那样完全缩小时，看到的是相对连贯的主世界。

cues.en: As you start to zoom in, you see bays, peaks, valleys, troughs.
cues.zh: 当你开始放大，你会看到海湾、山峰、山谷、洼地。

cues.en: And the great thing is this is actually really easy to implement. There's a lot of really good parallel and simplex libraries out there.
cues.zh: 实现起来其实非常简单。市面上有很多优秀的并行和单纯形库。

cues.en: Highly recommended. You can use it for anything, for making a pirate game with cool seas to sail around, or just building the overworld for your map. You can also use it if you want to generate
cues.zh: 强烈推荐。你可以用它做任何事，比如做个有酷炫海域可以航行的海盗游戏，或者只是构建地图的主世界。你也可以用它来生成

cues.en: realistic looking clouds, particles. You can even make wood grain with it with the right values.
cues.zh: 逼真的云朵、粒子。只要参数调对，甚至能做出木纹效果。

cues.en: And that brings me to one point that I can't emphasize enough.
cues.zh: 这就引出了我想强调的一点，怎么强调都不为过。

cues.en: You
cues.zh: 你

cues.en: very rarely need to use just one technique on a map.
cues.zh: 极少需要在同一张地图上只用一种技术。

cues.en: So here,
cues.zh: 所以这里，

cues.en: the top left, we've used WSP
cues.zh: 左上角，我们用了 WSP

cues.en: technique to produce a pretty linear looking dwarven fortress.
cues.zh: 技术，生成了一个看起来相当线性的矮人堡垒。

cues.en: On the right, cellular automata
cues.zh: 右边，元胞自动机

cues.en: has made a really open looking
cues.zh: 生成了一套非常开阔的

cues.en: sort of cavern system, might be a dangerous underworld. So, running with that theme,
cues.zh: 洞穴系统，可能是危险的地下世界。顺着这个主题，

cues.en: I simply took the left half of the dwarven fortress and the right half of the cellular automata,
cues.zh: 我直接把矮人堡垒的左半边和元胞自动机的右半边拼在一起，

cues.en: and you have what looks like a fortress that suddenly breaks out into a nasty underworld.
cues.zh: 就得到了一个看起来像是堡垒突然延伸进凶险地下世界的效果。

cues.en: Well, I thought
cues.zh: 不过我想

cues.en: a better theme for that might be that the dwarves were digging. They came to the underworld and they needed to protect themselves. So I added a prefab, a pre designed section in the middle, adding fortifications.
cues.zh: 更好的主题可能是矮人正在挖掘。他们挖到了地下世界，需要保护自己。于是我加了一个预制件，在中间预先设计好的区域，加上防御工事。

cues.en: And so with two very simple techniques, you've produced a map that actually tells a story rather than just being a bunch of random rooms.
cues.zh: 就这样，用两种非常简单的技术，你做出的地图就能讲一个故事，而不只是一堆随机的房间。

cues.en: Another popular combination
cues.zh: 另一个很受欢迎的组合

cues.en: is take a map and then use DLA to fire particles at it and blast parts of the map away. This starts to look like the dwarves failed to pay their maintenance bill or had a serious water problem,
cues.zh: 是拿一张地图，然后用DLA向它发射粒子，把地图的一部分炸掉。这开始看起来像矮人没付维护费，或者遇到了严重的漏水问题，

cues.en: as the map becomes more and more organic looking while keeping its basic structure.
cues.zh: 地图变得越来越有机，同时保留着基本结构。

cues.en: I mentioned prefabs before.
cues.zh: 我之前提到过预制体。

cues.en: Prefabs are a great idea. So you can make a massively random map,
cues.zh: 预制体是个好主意。这样你可以生成一张极度随机的地图，

cues.en: but if you start injecting human design elements into it, then you get the chance to really make the game your own.
cues.zh: 但如果你开始往里面注入人工设计的元素，你就有机会真正让游戏变成你自己的。

cues.en: So I've got a prefab here that is definitely not a trap. It's death traps surrounding a treasure chest. You've probably seen that in a lot of console RPGs.
cues.zh: 所以我这里有个预制体，绝对不是什么陷阱。是围绕宝箱的致命陷阱。你可能在很多主机RPG里见过这种。

cues.en: You enter a room, you see a chest with nothing guarding it, you can be pretty sure that something bad is about to happen to you.
cues.zh: 你走进一个房间，看到一个宝箱周围什么守卫都没有，你基本可以确定坏事要发生了。

cues.en: So the room structure
cues.zh: 所以房间结构

cues.en: makes it relatively easy to play as a prefab.
cues.zh: 让预制体的放置相对容易。

cues.en: You can go through the room list, find a room that's bigger than the prefab, and you know the prefab fits there.
cues.zh: 你可以遍历房间列表，找一个比预制体大的房间，就知道预制体能放进去。

cues.en: On a map that doesn't have rooms, it can be a little more tricky. What I usually do is I pick random locations,
cues.zh: 在没有房间的地图上，这会稍微棘手一些。我通常的做法是随机选位置，

cues.en: look and see if the prefab will fit, and place them. If it won't, then I don't place it there. And if I've got a nice big list of prefabs,
cues.zh: 看看预制体能不能放得下，然后放置。放不下就不放那儿。如果我有一份很大的预制体列表，

cues.en: then I'll keep going until I've added a few of them, and being careful not to add all of them so the game is different next time I play.
cues.zh: 那我就一直放，直到放进去几个为止，并且小心不要全部放完，这样下次玩的时候游戏就不一样了。

cues.en: Alright, very quick change of gears, because the next set of algorithms are all to
cues.zh: 好的，我们快速换个话题，因为接下来的这组算法都要

cues.en: rely on this one, Add Dijkstra maps.
cues.zh: 依赖这一个，加上 Dijkstra 地图。

cues.en: I highly recommend that you go to Rogue Basin and read the
cues.zh: 我强烈建议你去 Rogue Basin 读一读

cues.en: incredible power of Dijkstra maps on there. It is an excellent article.
cues.zh: 那里关于 Dijkstra 地图强大之处的精彩文章。那是一篇极好的文章。

cues.en: And Dijkstra maps are a very, very powerful tool. If you're into making roguelikes, I recommend that you learn about them.
cues.zh: Dijkstra 地图是非常非常强大的工具。如果你喜欢做 roguelike 游戏，我建议你学一学。

cues.en: To make them, you start with one or more starting points, in this case, the blue knight.
cues.zh: 要制作它，你从一个或多个起点开始，这里就是那个蓝色骑士。

cues.en: The rest of the map gets marked to a sentinel value, meaning you can't go there.
cues.zh: 地图的其余部分被标记为一个哨兵值，意思是你不能去那里。

cues.en: And then you look at all of the tiles adjacent to your starting point. If you can walk into them, you put a one on them. You get there now one step away from the starting point.
cues.zh: 然后你查看起点周围所有相邻的格子。如果能够走进去，就在上面标一个 1。这样你现在离起点只有一步了。

cues.en: Then you keep going. So, every
cues.zh: 然后继续。所以，每一个

cues.en: that... Every walkable tile that's next to a one gets a two, and a three, and a four, and a five. Eventually, you have a complete
cues.zh: 那个……每一个紧挨着 1 的可走格子都标上 2，然后是 3、4、5。最终，你就得到了一张完整的

cues.en: map that tells you, first of all, the sentinel value means
cues.zh: 地图，它首先告诉你，哨兵值意味着

cues.en: that you can't go there. So now you've got a list of all the cells you can't use.
cues.zh: 你不能去那里。所以现在你有了一个所有不能使用的格子的列表。

cues.en: Likewise, the
cues.zh: 同样地，

cues.en: numbered tiles tell you how far you are away from a starting point.
cues.zh: 带编号的格子告诉你离起点有多远。

cues.en: So the first big use for this is when you've generated something like cellular automata that can give you chunks of the map that you can't get to, pick a central point, find one that's open, generate a Dijkstra map,
cues.zh: 所以第一个大用途是，当你生成了类似细胞自动机的东西，它可能给你一些无法到达的地图区块时，选一个中心点，找一个开放的格子，生成一张 Dijkstra 地图，

cues.en: and then all of the tiles that are open but have the sentinel value on your Dijkstra map can't be reached. I've highlighted those in red on the map.
cues.zh: 然后所有开放但在你的 Dijkstra 地图上带有哨兵值的格子都是无法到达的。我在地图上用红色高亮了那些格子。

cues.en: You can delete those because nobody can get there. Or if you've got a map... If you've got a game system that encourages tunneling,
cues.zh: 你可以删掉那些地方，因为没人能到那儿。或者如果你有张地图……如果你的游戏系统鼓励挖通道，

cues.en: then go ahead and hide the stuff that needs to be reached with tunneling in those areas.
cues.zh: 那就把需要靠挖通道才能到达的东西藏在这些区域里。

cues.en: This can also help you with placing a starting point for your map.
cues.zh: 这也能帮你为地图放置起点。

cues.en: Making sure that you cull the
cues.zh: 确保你剔除掉

cues.en: unreachable areas before you pick a starting point ensures that you won't place the player somewhere that they can't get out of, and avoids the always embarrassing case of the map that's only got two tiles that you can actually walk on.
cues.zh: 不可达区域，然后再选起点，这样就不会把玩家放到出不去的地方，也能避免那种尴尬情况：地图上只有两个格能走。

cues.en: That has happened to me.
cues.zh: 我遇到过这种事。

cues.en: So, typically, to place a starting point, if I know that I want to be on the left, I'll
cues.zh: 所以通常放起点时，如果我知道我想放在左边，我会

cues.en: place somewhere in the middle on the left, and then I'll simply look around for a neighboring tile that is open and hasn't been culled by the Dijkstra map.
cues.zh: 放在左侧中间某个位置，然后就在周围找一个可通行、且没被 Dijkstra 图剔除的相邻格子。

cues.en: To find an endpoint, you can use the same thing if you want to go left to right. A lot of games
cues.zh: 要找终点，如果你想从左到右，也可以用同样的方法。很多游戏

cues.en: prefer to have more of a
cues.zh: 更喜欢更偏向

cues.en: structured progression.
cues.zh: 结构化的推进流程。

cues.en: Once you've culled the map, you know that anywhere on the map can be that is still open after you've removed the areas you can't get to, it's safe to place an exit. So you find
cues.zh: 一旦剔除了地图，你就知道，移除不可达区域后仍然可通行的地图上任何位置，放出口都是安全的。于是你找到

cues.en: the rough area you want to put the exit, and you place
cues.zh: 你想放出口的大致区域，然后把它放在

cues.en: on a nearby open tile.
cues.zh: 附近一个可通行的格子上。

cues.en: I've gone ahead and marked the optimal route through that map.
cues.zh: 我已经标出了穿过那张地图的最优路线。

cues.en: You can also, if you really dislike your player, use digster to find the least accessible part of the map and put the exit there. If they're starting in the middle, this is a really bad idea, because
cues.zh: 如果你真的很讨厌你的玩家，也可以用 digster 找出地图最难到达的部分，把出口放那儿。如果他们从中间开始，这真是个坏主意，因为

cues.en: three the quarters of the map is basically irrelevant.
cues.zh: 地图的四分之三基本就无关紧要了。

cues.en: However, if you want to hide something,
cues.zh: 不过，如果你想藏点东西，

cues.en: this is a great way to do it. Find the starting point, then find the least accessible point on the map, hide something there, and you force the player to go on a trailer hunt if they're going to get the bonus item.
cues.zh: 这可是个好办法。找到起点，再找到地图上最难到达的点，把东西藏在那儿，玩家要想拿到奖励道具，就得一路仔细搜寻。

cues.en: That leads to one of my favorite techniques for refining a map once you've generated it. I call it the hot path. Once you've got your start point and your end point, you generate the path between the two. I use a star. In this case, I think I used
cues.zh: 这就引出了我最喜欢的、在地图生成后进一步精修的技术之一。我称之为热路径。一旦确定了起点和终点，你就生成两点之间的路径。我用的是 A* 算法。在这个例子里，我记得用的是

cues.en: a Dijkstra map and just walked the
cues.zh: 一张 Dijkstra 图，然后直接沿

cues.en: distance between the two.
cues.zh: 两点之间的距离走。

cues.en: Then you make another Dijkstra map using all the points on the path as your hot path.
cues.zh: 然后你再生成一张 Dijkstra 图，把路径上的所有点都当作你的热路径。

cues.en: And then on that Dijkstra map, everything with a tile value of under, say, 10
cues.zh: 接着在那张 Dijkstra 图上，所有地块值低于比如 10 的地方

cues.en: is the hot path and is close, but not necessarily directly on the best path through the dungeon.
cues.zh: 就是热路径，离得近，但不一定正好在穿过地牢的最佳路径上。

cues.en: So what can you do with this? Well, if you prefer a less branchy game,
cues.zh: 那这能用来做什么呢？如果你想要一个分支更少的游戏，

cues.en: you can use it to remove the parts of the map that are completely irrelevant.
cues.zh: 可以用它把地图上完全无关的部分去掉。

cues.en: If your game involves a great deal of progression from, say, left to right,
cues.zh: 如果你的游戏涉及大量从比如左到右的推进，

cues.en: this is a good way to do it, and a good way to
cues.zh: 这就是个好办法，也是个好办法

cues.en: not force the player to explore huge,
cues.zh: 不让玩家去探索巨大、

cues.en: winding labyrinths with no real purpose to them.
cues.zh: 蜿蜒却毫无实际意义的迷宫。

cues.en: If you're using a room based generation,
cues.zh: 如果你用的是基于房间的生成方式，

cues.en: then this can be even more useful. I've marked in yellow the rooms that are on the hot path that go directly from point a to point b.
cues.zh: 那就更有用了。我用黄色标出了热路径上那些直接从 A 点到 B 点的房间。

cues.en: Well, so that means the gray rooms aren't really necessary.
cues.zh: 也就是说，灰色房间其实并非必需。

cues.en: Or are they? Maybe the gray rooms could be culled if you just want to have a go to room, go to room, go to room type of game.
cues.zh: 真的是这样吗？也许灰色房间可以删掉，如果你只想要那种“去这个房间、去那个房间、再去下一个房间”的游戏。

cues.en: Or the gray rooms could be where you hide bonus things.
cues.zh: 或者灰色房间可以用来藏额外奖励。

cues.en: You might have the yellow rooms mark some breadcrumbs to give the player a clue as to where to go,
cues.zh: 你可以让黄色房间标记一些线索，给玩家提示该往哪走，

cues.en: and teach them by putting really scary things in the gray area that going off the beaten path is only to be done once you're a little more experienced.
cues.zh: 并在灰色区域放些特别吓人的东西来教育他们：偏离主路这种事，得等你稍微有点经验了再干。

cues.en: You can also use this knowledge
cues.zh: 你也可以利用这些知识

cues.en: to order
cues.zh: 来安排

cues.en: the progression of a story.
cues.zh: 故事的推进顺序。

cues.en: So you know that if the player is going to go through this dungeon, they're probably going to go through one, nine.
cues.zh: 所以你知道，如果玩家要穿过这个地牢，他们大概会按一、九的顺序走。

cues.en: And that's
cues.zh: 这没

cues.en: okay. If you're telling a story, and let's say your grandfather tells you that it is your destiny to go out and save the world, he's probably going to want to tell you that somewhere around Room 1, so you can avoid the old windbag.
cues.zh: 问题。如果你在讲故事，比如说你爷爷告诉你，你的命运就是出去拯救世界，他大概会想在1号房间附近告诉你这件事，这样你就能避开那个老唠叨鬼了。

cues.en: Somewhere around two, somebody should show up and tell you that your destiny is futile, you should abandon it, give up,
cues.zh: 在2号房间附近，应该有人出现，告诉你你的命运是徒劳的，你应该放弃、别干了，

cues.en: and the whole adventuring thing isn't for you,
cues.zh: 冒险这档子事不适合你，

cues.en: and so on.
cues.zh: 诸如此类。

cues.zh: 另一种做法是，

cues.en: you might have decided that you want to do the old saw of the locked door that has a key somewhere on the map.
cues.zh: 你可能决定采用那个老套路：一扇锁着的门，钥匙藏在地图某处。

cues.en: Also,
cues.zh: 另外，

cues.en: posing that you've decided that Room 5 is going be where the locked door shall be, it would be a good choice because you can do a flood fill and discover that there's nowhere else, that there's no alternates to going through the exit from Room 5.
cues.zh: 假设你已经决定把锁着的门放在5号房间，这会是个好选择，因为你可以做一次洪水填充，发现没有别的路，除了从5号房间的出口出去之外没有其他选择。

cues.en: So you place a locked door there.
cues.zh: 所以你在这里放了一扇锁着的门。

cues.en: And now you absolutely know that the key has to be somewhere between Rooms 1 And 4 for this to be a solvable puzzle. It would really suck if you decided to spawn the key in Room 6 and leave yourself with
cues.zh: 现在你完全清楚，要想让谜题有解，钥匙必须放在 1 到 4 号房间之间。要是你把钥匙刷在 6 号房间，那就太坑了，因为你会留下

cues.en: a map that cannot be solved without finding some other way to open the door. Unless,
cues.zh: 一张除非另寻他法开门、否则根本无解的地图。除非，

cues.zh: 当然，这本就是你的目的。

cues.zh: 实际上，这

cues.en: the point of what I've been trying to say, is guide your randomness and then use algorithms to check your randomness to make sure that it matches what you want.
cues.zh: 正是我一直想表达的重点：引导你的随机性，然后用算法去检验它，确保它符合你的预期。

cues.en: The first one is from Darren Gray who asks,
cues.zh: 第一个来自 Darren Gray，他问，

cues.en: how do you make generated maps not look, you know, very samey? For example, he says that he can always notice when an overlook... Overworld
cues.zh: 怎么让生成的地图看起来不那么千篇一律？比如他说，他总能一眼看出某个俯瞰……Overworld

cues.en: is generated with Perlin noise.
cues.zh: 是用 Perlin 噪声生成的。

cues.en: Yeah. That's actually a fun one. I play Spot to Perlin.
cues.zh: 是的。这其实挺有意思。我就爱玩“找 Perlin”。

cues.en: One of the best things to do is to generate
cues.zh: 最好的做法之一是生成

cues.en: multiple noise maps and mix them together.
cues.zh: 多张噪声图，然后把它们混在一起。

cues.en: So, if you decided that this region is mountains,
cues.zh: 所以，如果你确定这个区域是山地，

cues.en: start mixing in
cues.zh: 就开始混入

cues.en: height values from another
cues.zh: 另一张高度图里的

cues.en: more mountainous looking
cues.zh: 更有山地感的

cues.en: height map. And that gets you something that as well as just going up, actually goes up and down, up and down, and starts to look more like mountains and less like a boring old gradient.
cues.zh: 高度值。这样得到的结果不只是往上走，而是上上下下、起伏不断，开始更像山脉，而不像无聊的旧梯度。

cues.en: You can also have a lot of fun generate your Perlin and then
cues.zh: 你还可以玩点花样：生成你的 Perlin，然后

cues.en: run something like erosion on it.
cues.zh: 在上面跑个侵蚀之类的处理。

cues.en: Running a simple erosion simulator,
cues.zh: 跑一个简单的侵蚀模拟器，

cues.en: especially if you decide that some rocks are harder than others, gives you a beautiful map in no time. I think that's how a world machine works.
cues.zh: 尤其是当你设定某些岩石比其他的更硬时，很快就能得到一张漂亮的地图。我觉得 World Machine 就是这么干的。
